titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spell 18, the tribunals, sections A–E
about: Spell 18 proper begins on Plate 13 of Ani's papyrus, after its introduction on Plate 12. In five sections, each opened in red, the spell names the gods of a tribunal in a holy place (Heliopolis, Busiris, Sekhem, Pe and Dep, and the Banks of Rekhty, a place not identified) and explains a night of the story of Osiris; each section closes with a refrain asking Thoth, who made Osiris true of voice against his enemies, to make Ani true of voice before the next tribunal. Other papyri open the spell with an address to Thoth that Ani's papyrus does not have (Budge supplies it from Naville's edition), and several signs and readings in this part are doubtful.

sentences.l: as-for · the-tribunal · great · which-is-in · Heliopolis · Atum · it-is · Shu · it-is · Tefnut · it-is
sentences.i: As for the great tribunal which is in Heliopolis: it is Atum, Shu and Tefnut.
sentences.n: Before this, Budge prints in square brackets a passage that Ani's papyrus does not have, supplied (his note) from Naville's edition of other papyri: the opening of the spell, an address to Thoth, who makes Osiris true of voice, and the start of the section on the tribunal in Heliopolis. It is left out, so Ani's text begins with the explanation of that tribunal. This is Budge's section A, and his line numerals start again at 1 in each of the five sections A–E. The papyrus writes ir ḏꜣḏꜣt ꜥꜣt imyt iwnw in red; the gods are black. ir 'as for' is the reed and the mouth: the particle that puts a noun first as the topic, which the rest of the sentence then explains. ḏꜣḏꜣt 'tribunal' is written as in the introduction: the fire-drill ḏꜣ (coded U28, approximate) twice, a small ring with ears between them (coded W24, approximate; not read), t, a barred sign (coded N1, approximate), and the seated god and a stroke as classifiers. ꜥꜣt 'great' is the column ꜥꜣ with the arm ꜥ (printed as a low bar, coded D36) as complement and t, feminine to agree with ḏꜣḏꜣt. imyt 'which is in' is the reed, the sign im with the owl m as complement, and t: the feminine of the nisba imy. iwnw 'Heliopolis' is the pillar iwn with the pot nw (a small eared ring, coded W24, approximate) and the town sign. Each god is followed by pw, 'it is': 'Atum it is, Shu it is, Tefnut it is', a sentence without a verb that says what the topic is. tmw 'Atum' is t, the sledge tm and the chick w with the seated god; šw 'Shu' is the feather šw with w and the god; tfnwt 'Tefnut' is t, the horned viper f, a ring marked with a cross (coded W24, approximate) for nw, t, and the cobra, the classifier of goddesses. Atum is the creator god of Heliopolis, and Shu and Tefnut are the first pair he brought into being.

sentences.l: as-for · guarding · the-rebels · were-destroyed · the-confederates · of-Seth · it-is · (m) · again(?) · was-beaten(?)-he
sentences.i: As for the guarding of the rebels: it is that the confederates of Seth were destroyed when he was beaten(?) again(?).
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir sꜣyw sbiw in red. sꜣyw is a looped upright crossed by a stick (coded Aa18, approximate), the sign sꜣ, with the vulture ꜣ as complement, two reeds y and the chick w, then a low hooked sign (coded U15) and a kneeling captive with one arm bent up to his head (coded A13) with a stroke as classifiers: read as the infinitive of sꜣw 'guard, keep watch over', the bound captive showing what kind of guarding this is (Budge: saiu, 'fettering'). sbiw 'the rebels' is s, the foot b, the reed and the chick w, with a thin stick (coded T14, approximate) and the captive as classifiers, as in Spell 1; it follows the infinitive as its object. ḥtm·n·tw is the wick ḥ, a tall upright with a small box at its foot (coded U33, approximate) read as tm, t and the owl m as complements, a long-legged bird (coded G27, approximate) and the sparrow of bad things as classifiers, then water n, t and the chick w: taken as the sḏm·n·tw·f, the passive of the past, 'were destroyed' (Budge reads one word, ḥetem-entu, 'the destruction'). The tall sign is not identified; in Spell 17 the same place in sḥtm 'destroy' holds a tall sign coded Q1. smꜣyw 'the confederates' is the lungs and windpipe smꜣ with ꜣ, two reeds, the seated god and a stroke (Budge: sami; his footnote gives a variant ḥait). stẖ 'Seth' is the bolt s, t and a plain rectangle (coded N37, approximate) for ẖ, with the god, as in Spell 17. pw after the clause makes it the explanation: 'it is (that) …'. nm is a slanting post (coded T34, approximate) with m as complement and the roll; Budge renders m nm 'the second time', and no other sense offers itself, so 'again' is taken from him with a query, and m is left untranslated in the literal line; this nm is not the interrogative nm 'who?'. qn·tw·f is the hill-slope q and water n with crossed sticks (coded Z9) and the sparrow as classifiers, then t, the coil w (Z7) and the viper ·f: the sḏm·tw·f, the passive, 'he was …'. The crossed sticks are the classifier of qnqn 'beat' in Spell 17, so qn is taken as 'beat, overpower'; Budge takes the clause as active, 'he wrought evil', which the tw does not allow. Both nm and qn are doubtful. The rebels are Seth's band, the murderers of Osiris, and their binding is their punishment.

sentences.l: O · Thoth · who-makes-true-of-voice · Osiris · against · enemies-his
sentences.i: O Thoth, who makes Osiris true of voice against his enemies,
sentences.n: The papyrus writes i in red. This is the refrain of the spell: it closes every section, each time naming the next tribunal. i 'O' is the reed with a kneeling man with his hand at his face (coded A2) as classifier, the gesture of calling out. ḏḥwty 'Thoth' is the ibis on its standard with t and two strokes y as complements. smꜣꜥ-ḫrw is the bolt s, the sickle mꜣ, the plinth mꜣꜥ (Aa11), the oar ḫrw and the chick w, with the man with hand to mouth: the participle 'who makes true of voice' of the causative of mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'true of voice', made with s; 'to make someone true of voice' is to win his case, and the phrase is kept literal, as in Spell 1. wsir 'Osiris' is the eye over the throne with the seated god. r 'against' is the mouth, the preposition of hostility. ḫftyw·f 'his enemies' is the placenta ḫ, the viper f, t and the vulture ꜣ (an old spelling, not read; Budge: χefta), the kneeling captive (coded A13) and a stroke as classifiers, and the viper ·f; the plural ending is not written. Thoth, the god of reckoning, keeps the record at the judgement, and as he won Osiris's case against Seth before the gods, he is asked to win Ani's.

sentences.l: make-true-of-voice · the-Osiris · Ani · (Ani) · against · enemies-his · before · the-tribunal · great · which-is-in · Busiris
sentences.i: make the Osiris Ani true of voice against his enemies before the great tribunal which is in Busiris
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ꜣny twice, at the end of line 3 and again at the head of line 4; read it once. Budge marks the second with '(sic)'. Both writings are shown, the first with the squatting man holding a flail (A52) as classifier, the second with the kneeling man with raised arm (A1), and the second is not translated. smꜣꜥ-ḫrw is written as in the address, without the classifier: here the imperative, 'make true of voice!'. wsir ꜣny 'the Osiris Ani' names the dead man as an Osiris, the god whose case was won; the god's classifier is written as for the god. ꜣny 'Ani' is the vulture ꜣ, water n with three strokes, and two reeds y with the classifier. m 'before' is the owl, the preposition 'in', here 'in the presence of' (at the same word in the next refrain Budge's footnote gives a variant m-bꜣḥ 'before'). ḏꜣḏꜣt and ꜥꜣt as in the first unit; imyt is here the reed, the sign im and t. ḏdw 'Busiris' is the djed pillar written twice, the chick w and the town sign: Djedu, the city of Osiris in the Delta. The refrain names the tribunal that the next section explains.

sentences.l: night · that · of · setting-up · the-djed-pillar · in · Busiris
sentences.i: on that night of setting up the djed pillar in Busiris.
sentences.n: grḥ 'night' is the jar-stand g, r and the wick ḥ with the sky and a hanging sceptre (coded N2, approximate) as classifier; it stands without a preposition, as the time when (Budge supplies '[on]'). pwy 'that' is p, w and two reeds, the demonstrative after its noun. n 'of' is water n, the genitive. sꜥḥꜥ 'setting up' is the folded cloth s and the post ꜥḥꜥ (P6) with the arm ꜥ as complement and the walking legs as classifier: the infinitive of the causative of ꜥḥꜥ 'stand', 'cause to stand'. ḏd 'the djed pillar' is the pillar itself with a stroke, the sign that is doubled in the name Djedu. m 'in' is the sign m (Aa15). The raising of the djed pillar was a rite of Osiris: the pillar stood for the god, set upright again after his death.

sentences.l: as-for · the-tribunal · great · which-is-in · Busiris · Osiris · it-is · Isis · it-is · Nephthys · it-is · Horus · it-is · who-protects · the-father
sentences.i: As for the great tribunal which is in Busiris: it is Osiris, Isis, Nephthys, and Horus, who protects the father.
sentences.n: Section B begins, and Budge's line numerals start again at 1; his footnote says that in many papyri the order of this and the following sections is changed. The papyrus writes ir ḏꜣḏꜣt ꜥꜣt imyt ḏdw in red. ꜥꜣt has t printed before the arm here. ꜣst 'Isis' is the seat ꜣs and t, with the egg (H8) and the cobra as classifiers. nbt-ḥwt 'Nephthys' is one sign, a basket on an enclosure (coded O9, approximate), with the cobra: 'Lady of the Mansion'. ḥr 'Horus' is the falcon alone. nḏ-ḥr is the sign nḏ (coded Aa27, approximate) with the pot nw (coded W24, approximate) as complement for n and a low hooked sign (U15) as classifier, then the face ḥr with its stroke: 'protect, take care of', literally 'guard the face of', as in Spell 17, here a participle, 'who protects'. itf 'the father' is t and the viper f alone, the word for father without its reed; no 'his' is written (Budge supplies it). Each name is again followed by pw. These are the family of Osiris: his sisters Isis and Nephthys, and his son Horus, who took up his cause.

sentences.l: as-for · the-setting-up · of-the-djed-pillar · in · Busiris · the-shoulder(?) · it-is · of · Horus · foremost · of-Sekhem
sentences.i: As for the setting up of the djed pillar in Busiris: it is the shoulder(?) of Horus, Foremost of Sekhem.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir sꜥḥꜥ ḏd m ḏdw in red. sꜥḥꜥ is written as in section A; ḏd 'the djed pillar' has the seated god as its classifier here, the pillar as a divine thing. qꜥḥ is the hill-slope q, the arm ꜥ and the wick ḥ, with the arm (D41), a stroke and a small loop with a tail (coded F51, approximate) as classifiers, as in Spell 1: 'shoulder', perhaps 'arm'; which part of the body is meant is not sure. n 'of' is the genitive. ḫnty 'foremost' is three jars in a rack (coded W17, approximate), ḫnt, with n and t as complements and two strokes y. sḫm 'Sekhem' is the sceptre sḫm (S42) with the placenta ḫ, the sign m (Aa15) and a flat sign with an upright loop (coded R22, as in Spell 1) as complements, and the house and the town sign as classifiers: the town of Horus north of Memphis that the Greeks called Letopolis. In Spell 1 Ani guards, with Horus, the left shoulder of Osiris which is in Sekhem.

sentences.l: they · around · Osiris · as · bandages · of · clothing
sentences.i: They are around Osiris as bandages of clothing.
sentences.n: iw·sn 'they are' is the reed and the chick w, the particle iw, with ·sn 'they', the bolt s and water n with plural strokes; iw is not translated, and the clause has no verb: 'they (are) around Osiris'. Who 'they' are is not said; perhaps the gods of the tribunal just named. ḥꜣ 'around, behind' is the papyrus clump ḥꜣ with ꜣ as complement and a small head (coded D1, approximate) as classifier, as in Spell 17. m 'as' is the owl. mrw is the hoe mr with r as complement and w, with a small looped cord (coded V6, approximate) and the low hooked sign as classifiers: read as mrw 'bandages', from a verb mr 'bind', which the cord suits (Budge: meru, 'bandages'). The word is not met elsewhere in these parts, and its sense rests on the classifier and on Budge. n 'of' is water n. ḥbs 'clothing' is the wick ḥ, the foot b and the folded cloth s, with the cord (V6, approximate) and plural strokes; Budge's numeral 3 is printed in the middle of the word, and the line is kept at 2. The wrapping of the body of Osiris, the first mummy, is the model for the wrapping of every dead person.

sentences.l: O · Thoth · who-makes-true-of-voice · Osiris · against · enemies-his
sentences.i: O Thoth, who makes Osiris true of voice against his enemies,
sentences.n: The papyrus writes i in red. The refrain again, as in section A; here smꜣꜥ-ḫrw has no chick w, and the oar is followed directly by the man with hand to mouth.

sentences.l: make-true-of-voice · the-Osiris · Ani · true-of-voice · against · enemies-his · before · the-tribunal · great · which-is-in · Sekhem
sentences.i: make true of voice the Osiris Ani, true of voice, against his enemies before the great tribunal which is in Sekhem
sentences.n: Ani's name is written once here. mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'true of voice' is the plinth mꜣꜥ (Aa11) over the oar ḫrw, without the sickle mꜣ: the epithet of the dead whose words were found true at the judgement, set after the name. ḫftyw·f is written without the vulture. m 'before' is the owl again (Budge's footnote: other copies have m-bꜣḥ). ḏꜣḏꜣt has plural strokes after the seated god; ꜥꜣt has t before the arm. sḫm 'Sekhem' has the owl m in place of Aa15. The refrain now names Sekhem, whose tribunal section C explains.

sentences.l: night · of · the-things · of-the-night · in · Sekhem
sentences.i: on the night of the things of the night in Sekhem.
sentences.n: No pwy 'that' is written this time. ḫt 'things' is the placenta ḫ and t with the roll and a stroke as classifiers. ḫꜣwy 'night, evening' is a plant on a stem with roots (coded M12, approximate) for ḫꜣ, two strokes y and the chick w, with the sky and its hanging sceptre (coded N2, approximate) as classifier: the time when night falls (Budge: χaui, 'night'). ḫt ḫꜣwy is a direct genitive, 'the things of the night', as in the address of Spell 125; 'things' are often offerings and rites, and which rites of the evening are meant is not said. m 'in' is the owl, and sḫm is written as in the previous unit.

sentences.l: as-for · the-tribunal · great · which-is-in · Sekhem · Horus-Khenty-irty · Thoth · it-is · who-are · in · the-tribunal · of-En-iarered-ef
sentences.i: As for the great tribunal which is in Sekhem: it is Horus-Khenty-irty and Thoth, who are in the tribunal of En-iarered-ef.
sentences.n: Section C begins, and Budge's line numerals start again at 1. The papyrus writes ir ḏꜣḏꜣt ꜥꜣt imyt sḫm in red. ḥr-ḫnty-irty is printed by Budge as two groups, which are joined here as one name, as in Spell 17: the falcon ḥr alone, then ḫnty 'foremost' (W17, approximate) with n, t and two strokes y; then the flat sign with an upright loop (coded R22) that writes ḫm in Sekhem; then the eye twice with the seated god, irty 'the two eyes', the second eye making the dual. Budge reads the loop sign àn (Ḥeru-χenti-àn-maa); it may stand for the ḫm of Sekhem, naming the god as the one of that town, or for something else, and it is left unread. The name is taken as Horus-Khenty-irty, 'Horus Foremost of the Two Eyes', as in Spell 17, the Horus of Sekhem. ḏḥwty 'Thoth' and pw as before; one pw serves both names. nty 'who' is water n, t and two strokes y, the relative adjective, written without a plural ending; it may refer to Thoth alone, 'who is'. m 'in' is the owl, and ḏꜣḏꜣt is written as before. n-iꜣrrd-f 'En-iarered-ef' is water n, the vulture and the reed (in that order), r twice, a cord with tails (coded T12, approximate) for rd, an open box as classifier and the viper f, here without the town sign (Budge: Naàrereṭef). It is the holy place of Osiris named in Spell 17; the meaning of the name is not sure.

sentences.l: as-for · night · that · of · the-things · of-the-night(?) · of-the-festival(?) · the-brightening · of-the-land · it-is · at · the-coffin · of-Osiris
sentences.i: As for that night of the things of the night(?) of the festival(?): it is the dawn at the coffin of Osiris.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir grḥ pwy n ḫt ḫꜣwt ḥb in red. ḫꜣwt is the plant ḫꜣ (coded M12, approximate) with ꜣ, w and t, then a short stroke over a small slanting wedge (coded N21, approximate). Each 'ir' unit in this spell takes up the night named at the end of the section before (sꜥḥꜥ ḏd m ḏdw in section B, sꜥḥꜥ ꜥꜣw n ḥr in section D), and the night named at the end of section B is grḥ n ḫt ḫꜣwy m sḫm. So the word is taken as the same ḫꜣwy 'night', here written with t and without the sky classifier, as Budge reads it (χaut, 'night'). As it stands, the group could also be ḫꜣwt 'altar, offering table', as in the introduction, and the reading is doubtful. The next group, the festival bowl ḥb (W3) over the sun, has no transliteration in Budge, who renders 'of the festival': it is read ḥb 'festival', with the sun as classifier as in Spell 17; how it joins the words before it is not clear, and the reading is doubtful. ḥḏ tꜣ 'the dawn' is the mace ḥḏ (coded T3, approximate) with the cobra ḏ as complement and the sun as classifier, then the flat land sign tꜣ: literally 'the brightening of the land', daybreak. pw 'it is'. r 'at' is the mouth. qrsw 'the coffin' is the hill-slope q, r and the bolt s, with the coffin (Q6) and the low hooked sign as classifiers, its w not written. The night ends at daybreak beside the coffin of Osiris: the watch over the dead god lasts until morning.

sentences.l: O · Thoth · who-makes-true-of-voice · Osiris · against · enemies-his
sentences.i: O Thoth, who makes Osiris true of voice against his enemies,
sentences.n: The papyrus writes i in red. The refrain again, written as in section A; Budge's numeral 3 falls before r.

sentences.l: make-true-of-voice · the-Osiris · the-scribe · Ani · against · enemies-his · before · the-tribunal · great · which-is-in · Pe · Dep
sentences.i: make the Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice against his enemies before the great tribunal which is in Pe and Dep
sentences.n: sš 'the scribe' is the scribe's palette with its water-pot and pen (Y3), Ani's title, set between wsir and the name. ḫftyw·f is again written without the vulture. pt 'Pe' is the stool p, t and the town sign; dpt 'Dep' is the hand d, p, t and the town sign (Budge: Pet and Ṭept). The t is written in both names, which are usually called Pe and Dep; no 'and' is written between them. Pe and Dep are the twin towns of Buto in the north-western Delta, an ancient seat of Horus. The refrain now names the tribunal of section D.

sentences.l: night · that · of · setting-up · the-pillars(?) · of · Horus · was-made-firm · for-him · the-inheritance · in · the-property · of-father-his · Osiris
sentences.i: on that night of setting up the pillars(?) of Horus, when the inheritance of the property of his father Osiris was made firm for him.
sentences.n: sꜥḥꜥ is written as in section A. ꜥꜣw is three upright columns with swelling capital and base, which match no sign exactly (coded O29, the column ꜥꜣ, approximate), written three times for a plural and read with Budge as ꜥꜣw (his āāiui, 'columns'). If the sign is the pillar iwn the word would be iwnw 'pillars'; the sense is the same, but the reading is doubtful. ḥr 'Horus' has the seated god here. smn·tw is the bolt s and the gaming board mn (Y5) with water n as complement, a tall sign with its top bent over (coded S38, approximate) and the roll as classifiers, then t and the chick w: smn 'make firm, establish', the causative of mn 'be firm', in the passive sḏm·tw·f, '(it) was made firm' (Budge: 'making him to be established'). It has no preposition before it and is taken as a clause of time, 'when …'. n·f 'for him' is water n and the viper. iwꜥt is a young lying animal (coded E9, approximate), iw, with w as complement, the arm ꜥ and t, with the roll and a stroke: iwꜥt 'inheritance', the noun from iwꜥ 'heir' (Budge: āuāt, 'heir'; the t and the roll of abstract things point to the inheritance rather than the heir). m 'in' is the owl. ḫt 'property' is ḫ and t with the roll over plural strokes. itf·f 'his father' is t and f, father without its reed, the seated man as classifier and the viper ·f. Horus's right to his father's inheritance is what he won in his long case against Seth before the gods.

sentences.l: as-for · the-tribunal · great · which-is-in · Pe · Dep · Horus · it-is · Isis · it-is · Imsety · it-is · Hapy · it-is
sentences.i: As for the great tribunal which is in Pe and Dep: it is Horus, Isis, Imsety and Hapy.
sentences.n: Section D begins, and Budge's line numerals start again at 1. The papyrus writes ir ḏꜣḏꜣt ꜥꜣt imyt pt dpt in red. imyt is here the reed and the sign im alone, its t not written. pt 'Pe' is written with t over p and a stroke. ꜣst 'Isis' has the egg but no cobra. msṯi 'Imsety' is the sign m (Aa15), the bolt s, the tethering rope ṯ and the reed, with the seated god, as in Spell 17 (Budge: Mesthà). ḥpy 'Hapy' is two stacked chevrons (coded Aa5, approximate) for ḥp, with p as complement, two reeds and the god (Budge: Ḥāpi). Imsety and Hapy are two of the four sons of Horus, who guard the inner organs of the dead.

sentences.l: as-for · the-setting-up · of-the-pillars(?) · of · Horus · the-saying · of-Seth · it-is · to · the-followers · set-up · pillars(?) · at-it
sentences.i: As for the setting up of the pillars(?) of Horus: it is what Seth said to the followers: 'Set up pillars(?) at it!'
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir sꜥḥꜥ ꜥꜣw n in red; ḥr after them is black. In sꜥḥꜥ the arm ꜥ is drawn through the foot of the post. ꜥꜣw 'pillars' (?) is the three upright columns, as in section C. ḏd 'saying' is the cobra ḏ with the hand d joined to it: the infinitive used as a noun, 'the saying of Seth', with stẖ after it as a direct genitive; stẖ is here the folded cloth s, t, the rectangle (coded N37, approximate) for ẖ and the god (Budge's footnote gives other spellings of the name). n 'to' is water n. imyw-ḫt 'the followers' is the reed, the sign im with m, w and a stroke, then the branch ḫt (M3) with ḫ and t as complements, the walking legs, and the seated man with a stroke: literally 'those who are in the following'; no 'his' is written (Budge supplies it). Then come Seth's words: sꜥḥꜥ is the imperative, 'set up!', and r·s is the mouth r with the bolt ·s, 'at it, by it'; the 'it' is feminine, and what it refers to is not said. The sense of the passage is not clear: the text does not say whose followers they are, or what 'it' is.

sentences.l: O · Thoth · who-makes-true-of-voice · Osiris · against · enemies-his
sentences.i: O Thoth, who makes Osiris true of voice against his enemies,
sentences.n: The papyrus writes i in red. The refrain again, written as in section A; Budge's numeral 3 is printed in the middle of ḫftyw·f, between the vulture and the captive, and the line is kept at 2.

sentences.l: make-true-of-voice · the-Osiris · the-scribe · Ani · true-of-voice · for-him(?) · against · enemies-his · before · the-tribunal · great · which-is-in · the-Banks(?) · of-Rekhty(?)
sentences.i: make true of voice the Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice for him(?), against his enemies before the great tribunal which is in the Banks(?) of Rekhty(?)
sentences.n: mꜣꜥ-ḫrw is again written without the sickle. After it stand water n and the viper, n·f 'for him, to him'; Budge renders 'is he', which n·f cannot mean. Perhaps the noun mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'vindication' is meant, with n·f, 'vindication (is) his'; perhaps the two signs are a slip. The rendering is doubtful. The place name is divided here into two words (Budge prints one group). iḏbw is three slanting wedges over three low bench-like signs, all coded N21 (approximate): the tongue of land iḏb 'bank', written three times for a plural, 'the Banks'. In Spell 1 the same sign over a canal writes iḏbwy 'the Two Banks', where the mourners of Osiris are. Budge reads the wedges Taiu(?), with his own query. rḫty is r, the placenta ḫ, t and two strokes y, then tall plants on a base (coded M20, approximate) and the town sign as classifiers (Budge: reχit). It is perhaps the place that Spell 1 writes rḫtt, Rekhtet, after the Two Banks. 'The Banks' is a fair reading of the signs, but the name and the place are not sure. The refrain names the tribunal of section E.

sentences.l: night · that · of · lying-down · of-Isis · awake-she · in · making · lament · for · brother-her · Osiris
sentences.i: on that night when Isis lay awake, making lament for her brother Osiris.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes kꜣbyt; read iꜣkbyt 'lament'. The group is the basket k, the vulture ꜣ, the foot b, two reeds y and t, with a curled lock of hair (coded D3) and a stroke: the signs of iꜣkbyt in Spell 1, with the lock of hair that classifies mourning, but without the reed and with k before ꜣ (Budge: kabit, 'lamentation'). The word can name the mourning woman as well as the mourning; after irt 'making' it is the lament. sḏr 'lying down' is the folded cloth s, a sign of stacked bars with a hook (coded M36, approximate), ḏr, with r as complement and a figure lying on a bed (A55) as classifier: the infinitive of sḏr 'lie down, spend the night', with ꜣst 'Isis' after it as its subject. rs·ti is a sign of joined pieces of wood (coded T13, approximate), rs, with the eye as classifier, then t and w: rs 'be awake, keep watch' in the stative, the ending 'she (is)' written tw (Budge: res-tu, 'watching'). ḥr irt 'making' is the face ḥr with its stroke and the eye ir with t: ḥr with the infinitive, 'in the act of making'. The second ḥr is 'for, on account of'. sn·s 'her brother' is the arrowhead sn (coded T22) with n, the seated man as classifier and the bolt ·s. Isis's watch beside her dead brother and husband is the model of the mourning for every dead person.

sentences.l: as-for · the-tribunal · great · which-is-in · the-Banks(?) · of-Rekhty(?) · Isis · it-is · Horus · it-is · Imsety · it-is
sentences.i: As for the great tribunal which is in the Banks(?) of Rekhty(?): it is Isis, Horus and Imsety.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ty for the name; read rḫty, as in the refrain just before: the second word is only tall plants on a base (M20, approximate), t, two strokes y and the town sign, and its r and ḫ are left out. Section E begins, and Budge's line numerals start again at 1. The papyrus writes ir ḏꜣḏꜣt ꜥꜣt imyt iḏbw rḫty in red. ꜥꜣt is followed here by the roll. iḏbw 'the Banks' is the three wedges (N21, approximate) alone, without the low signs beneath them. The name is as uncertain as in section D. ꜣst, ḥr and msṯi are written as in section D.

sentences.l: O · Thoth · who-makes-true-of-voice · Osiris · against · enemies-his
sentences.i: O Thoth, who makes Osiris true of voice against his enemies,
sentences.n: The papyrus writes i in red. The refrain for the last time on this plate, written as in section A.

sentences.l: make-true-of-voice · the-Osiris · the-scribe · Ani · true-of-voice · in · peace · against · enemies-his · before · the-tribunal · great · which-is-in · Abydos
sentences.i: make true of voice the Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice in peace, against his enemies before the great tribunal which is in Abydos
sentences.n: smꜣꜥ-ḫrw is written here in full, with w and the classifier. mꜣꜥ-ḫrw is again without the sickle. m ḥtp 'in peace' is the sign m (Aa15) and the loaf on a mat ḥtp (R4) alone: said of the dead who have come safely through the judgement. ꜣbḏw 'Abydos' is an ankh-like sign (coded S34, approximate) for ꜣb, with the foot b as complement, the low sign ḏw (coded N26, approximate), w and the town sign, as in Spell 17. Abydos was the holy city of Osiris, where his tomb was shown.

sentences.l: night · that · of · Haker · at · the-separating(?) · of-the-dead · at · the-inspecting · of-the-spirits · at · the-coming-into-being · of-jubilation(?) · in · Thinis
sentences.i: on that night of Haker, at the separating(?) of the dead, at the inspecting of the spirits, at the coming of jubilation(?) in Thinis.
sentences.n: hꜣkr 'Haker' is the reed-shelter h, the vulture ꜣ, the basket k and r, with the seated god as classifier (Budge: Haker): the name of a night festival of Osiris at Abydos, here classed as a god. m 'at' is the owl, three times. tnw is t, water n and the pot nw with w, then a forked upright pole (coded O30, approximate) with a bird with raised wings against it (coded G41, approximate), the roll and a stroke as classifiers: read as tnw from ṯni 'set apart, distinguish', which Spell 146 also writes with t (Budge: tennu, 'separation'). It could instead be tnw 'number, count', 'the counting of the dead'; the reading is doubtful. mtw 'the dead' is the owl m, t and w with the kneeling captive (coded A13) and a stroke: the dead who are condemned, classed with enemies. sipt 'the inspecting' is the folded cloth s, the reed i, the stool p and t with the roll: the noun of sip 'inspect, check' (Budge: sàpt, 'judgment'). ꜣḫw 'the spirits' is the crested ibis ꜣḫ with ḫ as complement, w, the squatting man with a flail (A52) and a stroke: the blessed dead. ḫpr 'the coming into being' is the scarab ḫpr with r. ihꜣbw is the reed i, the reed-shelter h, ꜣ, the foot b and w, with the man with hand to mouth (coded A2), the walking legs and plural strokes (Budge: àhabu, 'cries of joy'); the legs point to dancing and the hand at the mouth to shouting, and the word is taken as 'jubilation', with a query. tni 'Thinis' is t and water n, a tall staff hooked at the top (coded S39, approximate) taken as a classifier, two strokes y and the town sign (Budge: Teni): Teni, the old town near Abydos that the Greeks called Thinis. Plate 13 ends here, and the spell goes on on Plate 14.
